clue.text: Hellish hovel has big guy losing footing

parts.note: a sty is a filthy hovel, literally a pig's shelter

indicators.note: in an across clue the foot of a word is its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a giant is a very big guy

explanation.surface: A squalid hovel turns out to belong to a giant who has lost his footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing footing' drops the last letter of GIANT, leaving GIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian relates to the Styx, the river of the underworld, so it means hellish or infernally gloomy.

clue.text: Skill catching up with me coming up with fishy dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top
catching means holding inside, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: art is skill

explanation.surface: Skill picks up a cook who arrives with a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses everything, since in a down clue reading upward turns the letters round; 'catching' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is Japanese battered and fried seafood or vegetables, a classic fishy dish.

clue.text: Admit 28

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ..., the American general and President

explanation.definitionFit: To grant is to concede a point, and Ulysses S. Grant shares his first name with the answer at 28.

clue.text: Wearing a tie that's gone limp

indicators.note: gone means taken away, so the letters for that's are removed from tie

parts.note: taken as written
that's means i.e., which stands for 'that is'
limp means exhausted, tired

explanation.surface: Someone is wearing a tie that has gone limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes IE ('that is') from TIE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired means dressed, so in a garment or wearing it.

clue.text: Hole number dealing with bad habit

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
re means concerning or dealing with
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: Some number of people are working on a bad habit that leaves a hole in their lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or opening, a kind of hole in rock or a wall.

clue.text: Traveller heard deer in large numbers

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a roe is a deer, and many means a large number

explanation.surface: A traveller reports a large herd of deer.
explanation.walkthrough: ROE MANY said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany are the Roma people, traditionally nomadic, often called travellers in Britain.

clue.text: Unable to decide on house containing account books

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a villa is a house
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone can't make up their mind about a house containing account books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word here; the books are the New Testament, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacillant is a rare adjective meaning wavering, hesitating, indecisive.

clue.text: Bottom in semicircle to collapse

indicators.note: in places the bottom inside the half circle

parts.note: half of the word circle, its second half
the rump is the bottom

explanation.surface: A bottom drops into a semicircle of chairs, which then collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semicircle' gives only the latter half of CIRCLE, which 'in' wraps round RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple is to fold up or collapse suddenly.

clue.text: Potter story suffers cuts by being turned into comic strips

indicators.note: into puts the cuts inside the comics

parts.note: funnies are comic strips in newspapers
lops means cuts off

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A Beatrix Potter tale suffers cuts when adapted into comic strips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal and 'being turned' the reversal; 'suffers' is a link. 'Potter' means Beatrix Potter, not Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tale of the Flopsy Bunnies is one of Beatrix Potter's children's books.

clue.text: Austen's letter to old signaller

definitions.meaning: a novel by Jane Austen, the one about the matchmaking Miss Woodhouse
in the old military signalling alphabet the letter M was spoken this way

explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel, and in the pre-war signalling alphabet M was called Emma (as in 'pip emma').

clue.text: 28's boy to give us the facts about the little gentleman from Paris

indicators.note: the instructing phrase goes around the French gentleman, so 'about' signals one piece wrapping another

parts.note: to teach us is to give us the facts
LE is French for 'the', and M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a little gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to explain the facts about a small Parisian gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 28 is ULYSSES, whose son in Homer is the definition's 'boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Telemachus is the son of Odysseus (Ulysses in Latin) and Penelope in Homer's epic.

clue.text: Clothes with gold one of many to …

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Clothes trimmed with gold are worn by one of many hopefuls, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 13: Penelope, wife of Ulysses, was besieged by many suitors while he was away.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, and Penelope had over a hundred of them.

clue.text: … write "run away with me and forget 28"

definitions.text: … write "run away with me and forget 28"

parts.note: a pen is what you write with, so to pen is to write
to elope is to run away with a lover

explanation.surface: Continuing 12, a suitor writes asking his beloved to run off with him and forget her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 12, the whole clue describes Penelope, whose suitors begged her to forget her absent husband Ulysses (28).
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope, wife of Odysseus, was pressed by suitors to give up on her missing husband and marry again.

clue.text: There's still plenty of time for audience to Lady Gaga — years!

parts.note: an ear is a hearing, an audience (as in 'lend an ear')

indicators.note: gaga means crazy, so the word beside it is jumbled

parts.note: YS is an abbreviation of years

explanation.surface: A fan's message to the singer Lady Gaga: there's plenty of time for an audience — years!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaga' looks like part of the singer's name but is the anagram signal: LADY becomes LYDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'it's early days' says it is too soon to judge, that there is still plenty of time.

clue.text: One studying most of ancient Britons observes publicans

parts.note: L is a learner, one studying

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is cut

parts.note: the Iceni were the tribe of ancient Britons led by Boudicca
sees means observes

explanation.surface: A student of the ancient Britons watches the pub landlords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims ICENI to ICEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensees are holders of a licence to sell alcohol, i.e. pub landlords or publicans.

clue.text: Henry Cary, writer of 28

parts.note: Henry James is the American novelist, so Henry suggests his surname
Joyce Cary is the English novelist, so Cary suggests his first name

explanation.surface: A clue naming two writers, Henry and Cary, as the author of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The two novelists' names are split: Henry's surname and Cary's forename combine.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce wrote the 1922 novel Ulysses, the answer at 28.

clue.text: See 16
In which commander-in-chief should be 4?

parts.note: a commander-in-chief is in charge of everything, and 4 is ATTIRED, so the word wanted names both total command and a protective garment to be dressed in

explanation.definitionFit: Overall means in total charge, and overalls are a garment one may be dressed in.

clue.text: Where lion and unicorn finished up encouraging car use?

definitions.text: Where lion and unicorn finished up
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the lion and the unicorn are drummed off from the place where they fought
describing shopping centres built away from town centres, reachable mainly by car

explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme ends with the pair drummed out of town, and out-of-town retail parks are criticised for encouraging driving.

clue.text: It's about 28: say, is he queer?

indicators.note: say means the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: queer means odd, so the question is 'odd is he?'

explanation.surface: Someone asks about Ulysses whether he is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd is he' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odyssey is Homer's epic about Odysseus (Ulysses) and his voyage home.

clue.text: Court rendered mad by New Forester

parts.note: to woo is to court

indicators.note: rendered means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forester from the New Forest is driven mad by a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges MAD and N into DMAN. 'New Forester' suggests the New Forest, a woodland in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodman is a forester, someone who works in or looks after woods.

clue.text: Growing girl dropping to revolutionary spirit

indicators.note: dropping means losing the following word

parts.note: Topsy, the girl in Uncle Tom's Cabin, said she just growed
Che Guevara is the famous revolutionary

explanation.surface: A growing girl falls in with a revolutionary spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes TO from TOPSY, leaving PSY.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the soul or spirit, from the Greek word for breath.

clue.text: Court affair broadcast continuously by writer of 28

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the game's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: tennis is a game played on a court
on means without stopping, as in 'carried on'

explanation.surface: A tennis match on court is broadcast without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a royal court or a legal one, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson wrote the poem 'Ulysses', with its famous closing line about striving and not yielding.

clue.text: Consent of some whose reports show barbarians

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: ya is the informal yes used by some speakers, followed by the word whose

explanation.surface: Some people's reports show how barbarians gave their consent.
explanation.walkthrough: YA (yes) and WHOSE said together give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yahoos are the brutish humanoid creatures in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, and the word now means boorish louts.

clue.text: Pigeon for writer of 20

definitions.meaning: a homing pigeon is called a ...
the ancient Greek poet credited with the epic at 20

explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, and Homer is the poet of the Odyssey.

clue.text: War secrets disclosed that have pungent taste

indicators.note: secrets disclosed are let out and spread around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wartime secrets are leaked that leave a bitter taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disclosed' looks like a plain verb about leaks, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercress is a salad plant whose leaves have a sharp peppery bite.

clue.text: Jane Russell's version of 10

definitions.note: the part played by the actress Jane Russell in the 1953 film The French Line

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, the Austen novel

explanation.surface: The actress Jane Russell gives her own take on an Austen heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges the answer at 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Mame Valentine was the character played by Jane Russell in the film The French Line.

clue.text: Much of summer season not on, they say, for traveller

indicators.note: most of the month's name is kept, dropping its first letter

parts.note: July is a summer month

indicators.note: said aloud, the remaining letters sound like the needed ending

parts.note: the word season with its last two letters, the word on, taken away, leaving the plural of sea

explanation.surface: Much of the summer season is off, people say, for someone on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of' keeps most of JULY, dropping the J; 'they say' turns the sea word into the sound of the closing SSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses, the Latin Odysseus, wandered for ten years on his way home from Troy, the archetypal traveller.

clue.text: Monster not reduced following fire?

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed monster killed by Hercules

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so a letter is cut from the word

explanation.surface: A monster that is not shrunk follows a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts O from NOT, leaving NT. The definition is cryptic: it is the fire hydrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrant is the street water point firefighters use, so it is linked with fire, as in 'fire hydrant'.
